segments.label: Mo
segments.text: [warmly] And we're back. It's twelve forty on Night Radio, and line two has been blinking for ten minutes. Bram, are you there?

segments.label: Bram
segments.text: [clears throat] I'm here, I'm here. Is this the radio? Am I on the radio?

segments.label: Mo
segments.text: You're on the radio, Bram. What's happening at the lighthouse tonight?

segments.label: Bram
segments.text: Well. [sighs] The light went out. Not broken, mind you. It just... stopped. Like it wanted a nap.

segments.label: Mo
segments.text: Pip, please. Bram, did you try turning it off and on again?

segments.label: Bram
segments.text: [offended] Young man, I have kept that light for forty years. Of course I tried that.

segments.label: Pip
segments.text: [excited] Ooh, ooh, I know! Play it a song! Lighthouses love songs.

segments.label: Mo
segments.text: [laughs] Pip, cue the lullaby. Bram, hold the phone up to the lamp.

segments.label: Bram
segments.text: [far from the phone] It's... it's flickering. It's coming back! Would you look at that!

segments.label: Mo
segments.text: [softly] There you have it, night owls. Even lighthouses need a song sometimes. Goodnight, Bram.

segments.label: Bram
segments.text: [chuckles] Goodnight, you lot. Keep the music coming.
